subject: read the full property-management agreement
preheader: the recurring percentage may not include every service or fee.
headline: Model the management scope, not just one percentage.
body: A recurring management percentage may cover only the services listed in the agreement. Do not assume it includes lease-up, renewals, inspections, advertising, maintenance coordination, notices, court work, or other administration.

Ask how leasing and renewal charges are calculated, when they apply, and whether early turnover changes them. Convert fixed or event-based charges into separate scenarios using the expected tenancy assumptions.
Review maintenance markups, minimum charges, inspection fees, advertising, vacancy-period fees, termination terms, and any vendor relationships directly in the proposed agreement.

For illustration, changing an entered management assumption from 8% to 12% on $2,000 monthly rent changes modeled cost by $80 per month or $960 per year. That does not establish a typical fee or predict the property's return.

TrueCap starts a new analysis with a generic 8% management assumption. Replace it with the proposed management agreement and add any leasing, renewal, maintenance-markup, or administrative costs that are not included in that percentage.
